source_text: ⸀Καθὼς γέγραπται ἐν ⸂τῷ Ἠσαΐᾳ τῷ προφήτῃ⸃· ⸀Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν ⸀σου·
english_snapshot: Just as it is written in Isaiah the prophet: ‘Behold[a], I send my messenger before your face[c][b], who will prepare your way.’

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “in the prophets” instead of “in Isaiah the prophet.”

source_text: ⸀καὶ ⸀ὀργισθεὶς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ⸂αὐτοῦ ἥψατο⸃ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι·
english_snapshot: And being angry[a], he stretched out his hand, touched him, and said to him, “I am willing; be cleansed.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read “moved with compassion” instead of “being angry.”

source_text: καὶ ἐποίησεν ⸀δώδεκα, ἵνα ὦσιν μετ’ αὐτοῦ καὶ ἵνα ἀποστέλλῃ αὐτοὺς κηρύσσειν
english_snapshot: And he appointed twelve[a], so that they might be with him and so that he might send them out to preach[b],

signals.text: Some manuscripts add, 'whom he also named apostles.'

source_text: ὃς δ’ ἂν βλασφημήσῃ εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον, οὐκ ἔχει ἄφεσιν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, ἀλλὰ ἔνοχός ἐστιν αἰωνίου ⸀ἁμαρτήματος.
english_snapshot: but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness[c][b][a], but is guilty of an eternal sin.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'eternal judgment' or 'eternal condemnation' instead of 'eternal sin.'

source_text: Καὶ ἦλθον εἰς τὸ πέραν τῆς θαλάσσης εἰς τὴν χώραν τῶν ⸀Γερασηνῶν.
english_snapshot: And they came to the other side of the sea[a], to the region of the Gerasenes.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'Gadarenes'; others read 'Gergesenes.'

source_text: ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης ἐφοβεῖτο τὸν Ἰωάννην, εἰδὼς αὐτὸν ἄνδρα δίκαιον καὶ ἅγιον, καὶ συνετήρει αὐτόν, καὶ ἀκούσας αὐτοῦ πολλὰ ⸀ἠπόρει, καὶ ἡδέως αὐτοῦ ἤκουεν.
english_snapshot: For Herod feared John[a], knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and he kept him safe. And when he heard him, he was greatly perplexed, and yet he listened to him gladly.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read 'he did many things' instead of 'he was greatly perplexed.'

source_text: καὶ εἰσελθούσης τῆς θυγατρὸς ⸂αὐτῆς τῆς⸃ Ἡρῳδιάδος καὶ ὀρχησαμένης ⸂καὶ ἀρεσάσης⸃ τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ καὶ τοῖς συνανακειμένοις, ⸂εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεὺς⸃ τῷ κορασίῳ· Αἴτησόν με ὃ ἐὰν θέλῃς, καὶ δώσω σοι·
english_snapshot: And when Herodias's daughter came in and danced[a], and pleased Herod and those reclining at the table with him, the king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want[b], and I will give it to you.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts/traditions are understood as 'his daughter Herodias' rather than 'Herodias's daughter.' The Greek text followed here reads 'Herodias's daughter.'

source_text: καὶ ἀπ’ ⸀ἀγορᾶς ἐὰν μὴ ⸀βαπτίσωνται οὐκ ἐσθίουσιν, καὶ ἄλλα πολλά ἐστιν ἃ παρέλαβον κρατεῖν, βαπτισμοὺς ποτηρίων καὶ ξεστῶν καὶ χαλκίων ⸂καὶ κλινῶν⸃—
english_snapshot: And when they come from the marketplace[a], they do not eat unless they wash themselves[b], and there are many other things that they have received to keep: washings of cups and pitchers and copper vessels and dining couches—

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'and dining couches.'

source_text: Εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
english_snapshot: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic versions, but is present in the Byzantine majority tradition, the Latin tradition, and most Syriac witnesses. It is likely a later scribal addition echoing the identical phrase found earlier in Mark 4:9 and 4:23.

source_text: εἶτα πάλιν ⸀ἐπέθηκεν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸂διέβλεψεν καὶ ἀπεκατέστη καὶ ἐνέβλεπεν⸃ τηλαυγῶς ⸀ἅπαντα.
english_snapshot: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes[a], and he saw clearly and was restored[b], and he was seeing everything distinctly.

signals.text: Some manuscripts read wording reflected in translations such as 'and he looked intently and was restored, and saw everything clearly.'

source_text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ⸀εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ λέγων· Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην ⸀εἰσέλθῃς.
english_snapshot: And he sent him to his home[a], saying, “Do not even enter the village.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts add, “and do not tell anyone in the village.”

source_text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτο τὸ γένος ἐν οὐδενὶ δύναται ἐξελθεῖν εἰ μὴ ἐν ⸀προσευχῇ.
english_snapshot: And he said to them[a], “This kind cannot come out by anything except prayer.”

signals.text: Some later manuscripts read, “prayer and fasting.”

source_text: ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ, καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.
english_snapshot: where[a] their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations, but is present in the 5th-century Alexandrinus, the Latin tradition, and the later Byzantine majority. It is likely a later scribal addition that repeats the identical phrase from verse 48.

source_text: ὅπου ὁ σκώληξ αὐτῶν οὐ τελευτᾷ, καὶ τὸ πῦρ οὐ σβέννυται.
english_snapshot: where[a] their worm does not die, and the fire is not quenched.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations, but is present in the Byzantine majority tradition and the Latin tradition. It is likely a later scribal addition repeating the identical words of verse 48 (and verse 44).

source_text: Πᾶς γὰρ πυρὶ ⸀ἁλισθήσεται.
english_snapshot: For everyone will be salted with fire[a][b].

signals.text: Some manuscripts add, 'and every sacrifice will be salted with salt.'

source_text: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἐθαμβοῦντο ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις αὐτοῦ. ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τέκνα, πῶς δύσκολόν ⸀ἐστιν εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ εἰσελθεῖν·
english_snapshot: But the disciples were astonished at his words. Jesus answered again and said to them[a], “Children, how difficult it is to enter the kingdom of God!”

signals.text: Some manuscripts read, 'Children, how difficult it is for those who trust in riches to enter the kingdom of God.'

source_text: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, πάντα ὅσα ⸂προσεύχεσθε καὶ αἰτεῖσθε⸃, πιστεύετε ὅτι ⸀ἐλάβετε, καὶ ἔσται ὑμῖν.
english_snapshot: For this reason I tell you[a], whatever you pray and ask for, believe that you have received it[b], and it will be yours.

signals.text: Some manuscripts/readings are understood or rendered as 'believe that you receive them' rather than 'believe that you have received them.' The Greek text used here reads 'have received,' preserving the completed-action sense.

source_text: Εἰ δὲ ὑμεῖς οὐκ ἀφίετε, οὐδὲ ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς ἀφήσει τὰ παραπτώματα ὑμῶν.
english_snapshot: But[a] if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive your trespasses.

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including the 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic versions, but is present in the Byzantine majority tradition, the Latin tradition, and most Syriac witnesses. It was likely added by later scribes to harmonize with Jesus's words in Matthew 6:15.

source_text: ⸂ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃ ὅτι Πρώτη ⸀ἐστίν· Ἄκουε, Ἰσραήλ, κύριος ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν κύριος εἷς ἐστιν,
english_snapshot: Jesus answered[a], “The first is: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God[b], the Lord is one.

signals.text: Because this line quotes the Shema (Deut 6:4), “Lord” here reflects the Greek κύριος used in the Septuagint for the divine name YHWH.

source_text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Τοῦτό ἐστιν τὸ αἷμά μου ⸀τῆς διαθήκης τὸ ⸂ἐκχυννόμενον ὑπὲρ πολλῶν⸃.
english_snapshot: And he said to them[a], “This is my blood of the covenant[c][b], which is poured out for many.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts and parallel passages read 'my blood of the new covenant.' Mark's Greek text here is best read as 'my blood of the covenant.'

source_text: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο λέγων· ⸂Οὔτε οἶδα οὔτε ἐπίσταμαι σὺ τί⸃ λέγεις, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω εἰς τὸ προαύλιον ⸂καὶ ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν⸃.
english_snapshot: But he denied it[a], saying, “I neither know nor understand what you are saying.” And he went out into the forecourt, and a rooster crowed.

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit: 'and a rooster crowed.'

source_text: ὁ δὲ πάλιν ἠρνεῖτο. καὶ μετὰ μικρὸν πάλιν οἱ παρεστῶτες ἔλεγον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ Γαλιλαῖος εἶ ⸂καὶ ἡ λαλιά σου ὁμοιάζει⸃·
english_snapshot: But he again denied it[a]. And after a little while, those standing nearby again were saying to Peter, “Surely you are one of them, for you are also a Galilean[b], and your speech is similar.”

signals.text: Some manuscripts omit 'and your speech matches it.'

source_text: Καὶ ἐπληρώθη ἡ γραφὴ ἡ λέγουσα, Καὶ μετὰ ἀνόμων ἐλογίσθη.
english_snapshot: And[a] the scripture was fulfilled that says, "And he was numbered with the transgressors."

signals.text: This verse is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts (including 4th-century Sinaiticus and Vaticanus) and early Coptic translations, but is preserved in the Byzantine majority tradition and the Latin tradition. It was likely added by later scribes as a harmonization to Luke 22:37, which quotes Isaiah 53:12.

source_text: καὶ τῇ ⸂ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ⸃ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ ⸀μεγάλῃ· Ἐλωῒ ἐλωῒ ⸀λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι; ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ θεός μου ὁ θεός μου, εἰς τί ⸂ἐγκατέλιπές με⸃;
english_snapshot: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice[a], “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which is translated, “My God, my God[c][b], for what reason have you forsaken me?”

signals.text: Some manuscripts and many English traditions reflect the Semitic phrase as 'lama sabachthani' rather than 'lema sabachthani.'

source_text: καὶ ἐξελθοῦσαι ἔφυγον ἀπὸ τοῦ μνημείου, εἶχεν ⸀γὰρ αὐτὰς τρόμος καὶ ἔκστασις· καὶ οὐδενὶ οὐδὲν εἶπαν, ἐφοβοῦντο ⸁γάρ. ⟦Πάντα δὲ τὰ παρηγγελμένα τοῖς περὶ τὸν Πέτρον συντόμως ἐξήγγειλαν. μετὰ δὲ ταῦτα καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς καὶ ἄχρι δύσεως ἐξαπέστειλεν δι’ αὐτῶν τὸ ἱερὸν καὶ ἄφθαρτον κήρυγμα τῆς αἰωνίου σωτηρίας. ἀμήν.⟧
english_snapshot: And they went out and fled from the tomb[a], for trembling and astonishment had seized them. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

signals.text: Some manuscripts add the so-called shorter ending: 'And they reported briefly to those around Peter all that they had been commanded. And after these things, Jesus himself also sent out through them, from east to west, the sacred and imperishable proclamation of eternal salvation. Amen.'

source_text: ⟦Ἀναστὰς δὲ πρωῒ πρώτῃ σαββάτου ἐφάνη πρῶτον Μαρίᾳ τῇ Μαγδαληνῇ, ⸀παρ’ ἧς ἐκβεβλήκει ἑπτὰ δαιμόνια.
english_snapshot: After he had risen[a], early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom he had cast out seven demons.

signals.text: Verses 9–20 are absent from some early manuscripts of Mark; other manuscripts include them, sometimes with variation.

source_text: ⸀ὄφεις ἀροῦσιν κἂν θανάσιμόν τι πίωσιν οὐ μὴ αὐτοὺς βλάψῃ, ἐπὶ ἀρρώστους χεῖρας ἐπιθήσουσιν καὶ καλῶς ἕξουσιν.
english_snapshot: They will pick up snakes[a], and if they drink anything deadly, it will certainly not harm them; they will lay hands on the sick[d][c][b], and they will recover.

signals.text: Some early manuscripts do not include Mark 16:9–20; this verse belongs to the longer ending of Mark.
